purpose: Editorially selected Signals candidates for the Sunday 16 August 2026 edition. Only the URLs below may be promoted; each promoted row receives final editorial significance before publication.

topics.editorialRationale: Select NIST's AI-enabled vulnerability-management consultation. It turns the AI discussion into an operating question: whether automation can improve asset and vulnerability decisions without obscuring data quality, intervention authority or accountability.

No new market-structure candidate is promoted. The current queue contains potentially relevant CFTC items, but none adds enough verified EMEA leadership value to displace the existing reviewed evidence this week.

Select the Bank of England working paper on cloud-service-provider concentration. It is research rather than a new rule, but it gives financial-services leaders a strong current basis to test shared dependencies, substitutability and fallback evidence.
No new resilience candidate is promoted. The NCSC response is valuable context for the AI capability story, but is not duplicated as a separate public signal.
No new financial-crime candidate is promoted. The queue is dominated by individual enforcement and fraud notices that do not justify a new cross-firm operating call this week.
No new cyber candidate is promoted. Retain the active-exploitation priority rather than elevating a second item without a stronger direct management implication.
No new technology-failure candidate is promoted. Retain the reviewed failure and recovery evidence rather than promoting an already-covered incident.

Select the ICO's ACRO reprimand because it offers a current, official read-across on cyber security, personal-data handling and the evidence required to show that corrective action has closed the gap.
